def-qnt-expectile.title: Expectiles and expectile regression
def-qnt-expectile.html:
For τ∈(0,1) define the asymmetric squared loss ρτE(u)=|τ−1{u<0}|u2={τu2,u≥0,(1−τ)u2,u<0.{#eq-qnt-expectile-loss}

For a random variable Y with EY2<∞, the τ-expectile μτ is a minimizer of S(μ)=EρτE(Y−μ). The expectile regression model at level τ asserts that the τ-expectile of the conditional law of Y is 𝛃x⊤βτ, and the estimate is 𝛃β^τE∈argminb∑i=1nρτE(yi−x(i)⊤b).{#eq-qnt-expectile-sample}

def-qnt-gamlss.title: Generalized additive model for location, scale and shape
def-qnt-gamlss.title_html: Generalized additive model for location, scale and shape
def-qnt-gamlss.html:
Let D(θ1,…,θK) be a family of distributions on the response space with density or mass function d(y;θ1,…,θK); in this chapter θk denotes the kth parameter of that family, not the natural parameter of @def-glm-model. A GAMLSS asserts that the responses Y1,…,Yn are independent with Yi∼D(θi1,…,θiK),gk(θik)=ηik,k=1,…,K, where each gk is a strictly increasing link mapping the admissible range of θk onto R (the identity for an unrestricted parameter, the logarithm for a positive one, the logit for one in (0,1)), and each ηik is a structured additive predictor (@def-add-star) 𝛄ηik=β0k+∑j=1Jkfjk(vij),fjk(⋅) represented by Zjkγjk,{#eq-qnt-gamlss-predictor}

with each 𝛄γjk carrying a quadratic penalty 𝛄𝛄λjkγjk⊤Pjkγjk. The predictors for different parameters may use different covariates and different amounts of structure.

def-qnt-quantile.title: Check loss and quantile regression
def-qnt-quantile.html:
For τ∈(0,1) the check function is ρτ(u)=u{τ−1{u<0}}={τu,u≥0,(τ−1)u,u<0,{#eq-qnt-check}

a convex, piecewise linear, nonnegative function with a kink at the origin, equal to |u|/2 when τ=1/2. The linear quantile regression model at level τ asserts 𝛃QY(τ∣x)=x⊤βτ, and given data (yi,x(i)), i=1,…,n, a τ-regression quantile is any minimizer 𝛃β^τ∈argminb∈RpRτ(b)=∑i=1nρτ(yi−x(i)⊤b).{#eq-qnt-sample}

def-qnt-score.title: Scoring rule, propriety
def-qnt-score.html:
A scoring rule is a function S(F,y) assigning a penalty when the predictive distribution F is issued and the value y is observed; smaller is better. Write S(F,G)=EY∼GS(F,Y) for its expectation when Y really follows G. The rule is proper relative to a class of distributions if S(G,G)≤S(F,G)for all F,G in the class,{#eq-qnt-proper}

and strictly proper if equality forces F=G. A consistent scoring function for a functional T is a function s(x,y) with EGs{T(G),Y}≤EGs(x,Y) for every x; a functional admitting one is called elicitable.

exm-qnt-compare.title: Mean model, quantile model and GAMLSS on Engel’s budgets
exm-qnt-compare.title_html: Mean model, quantile model and GAMLSS on Engel’s budgets
exm-qnt-compare.html:
The 235 households are split into ten folds. On each fold, three predictive distributions are built from the other nine:

  1. the homoscedastic linear model of Part II, with normal errors and one σ^;

  2. quantile regressions at 199 levels τ=1/200,…,199/200, sorted at each covariate value by @prp-qnt-crossing(b) so that the fitted quantiles are ordered;

  3. the location-scale GAMLSS of @exm-qnt-engel-gamlss.

All three are scored the same way, by the discretized form of @eq-qnt-crps-check over that grid of levels, so no model is helped by a formula the others do not get.

model CRPS pinball 0.1 pinball 0.5 pinball 0.9 below q^0.1 below q^0.9
mean model 59.34 20.41 38.98 21.76 0.030 0.923
quantile model 53.00 17.69 38.05 14.93 0.089 0.902
GAMLSS 53.12 16.26 37.53 16.49 0.140 0.885

Scores are in francs, and each model gets its own best predictive distribution: for the mean model the exact t predictive of Section 12.3. Both distributional models beat it by about 6 francs of CRPS per household: the differences are −6.35 with a paired standard error of 1.75, and −6.23 with standard error 2.12. Against each other they differ by −0.12 with a paired standard error of 1.99, which is no difference at all. The mean model fails where @prp-qnt-beyond-mean predicted, putting only 0.030 of the households below its own tenth percentile.

The Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance of the held-out transforms from uniformity is 0.098 for the mean model, 0.024 for the quantile model and 0.055 for the GAMLSS (Figure 45.6.1). The mean model’s hump is the signature of predictive distributions that are too wide; the GAMLSS histogram is raised at both ends, the signature of a normal shape where the data want heavier tails — an actionable criticism, whose answer is a three-parameter family.

exm-qnt-coverage.title: Which interval keeps its promise
exm-qnt-coverage.html:
Generate n=150 observations from y=1+x+(0.2+1.2x)ε with x uniform on (0,2) and ε standard normal, so the true slope of the τ-quantile is 1+1.2zτ: 1.000 at the median, 2.538 at τ=0.9. Over 800 replicates (150 for the bootstrap, B=99), the nominal 95% intervals cover:

method τ=0.5 τ=0.9
iid formula 0.899 0.911
sandwich 0.965 0.911
pairs bootstrap 0.933 0.940

The iid formula undercovers at both levels, as it must. The sandwich is conservative at the median (mean width 0.989 against 0.743) and no better than the iid formula at τ=0.9, where its kernel estimate of D1 is fed by few residuals near zero. The bootstrap is the steadiest, at B extra linear programs.

exm-qnt-crossing-engel.title: Where Engel’s lines cross
exm-qnt-crossing-engel.html: The seven fitted lines of @exm-qnt-lp are not parallel, so every neighbouring pair crosses somewhere: at incomes of 252, 203, 163, 228, −117 and 143 francs. The smallest income in the data is 377, so every crossing lies outside the data, where the model was never tested (Figure 45.3.1(b)). Crossing reaches inside when the predictor is more flexible: adding a quadratic term in income leaves the curves out of order on 0.035 of a grid spanning the lowest 99% of incomes, beginning at the very edge. Rearranging repairs the ordering and moves the curves by at most 4.0 francs.

exm-qnt-engel-bands.title: Engel’s budgets, one more time
exm-qnt-engel-bands.html:
Engel’s 1857 survey of 235 Belgian working-class households records annual income and annual food expenditure; the same data supported the diagnostics of Chapter 20 and the tests of Section 21.2. Least squares gives a slope of 0.4852 and a single residual standard deviation of 114.1 francs. Split the households into thirds by income: the residual standard deviations within the thirds are 48.6, 74.8 and 171.6 francs, a ratio of 3.53 from the poorest third to the richest.

The consequence for a prediction interval is immediate. The nominal 95% interval from the homoscedastic normal model contains 1.000 of the poorest third, 1.000 of the middle third and 0.911 of the richest — far too wide where the data are tight and too narrow where they are loose — while the overall figure of 0.970 looks respectable. Averaging over the design hides the error that matters to each household.

Shape moves too. The quartile coefficient of skewness, (q0.75+q0.25−2q0.5)/(q0.75−q0.25), is −0.23 for the residuals of the poorest fifth of households and 0.40 for the richest fifth, and the interquartile range grows by a factor of 3.75 between them (Figure 45.1.1).

exm-qnt-engel-expectiles.title: Expectile lines for Engel’s budgets
exm-qnt-engel-expectiles.html:
The same 235 households, fitted at the same seven levels by @eq-qnt-expectile-sample:

τ 0.05 0.10 0.25 0.50 0.75 0.90 0.95
slope 0.3617 0.3830 0.4293 0.4852 0.5454 0.6017 0.6322
intercept 157.9 162.6 159.0 147.5 128.8 109.0 99.8

The level τ=1/2 reproduces least squares exactly, slope 0.4852. The fan opens in the same direction as the quantile fan of @exm-qnt-lp but less widely, from 0.3617 to 0.6322 against 0.3434 to 0.7091 — not a discrepancy, since by @exm-qnt-expectile-levels the level 0.9 means a more central position for an expectile.

exm-qnt-engel-gamlss.title: Mean and scale together
exm-qnt-engel-gamlss.html:
Take @eq-qnt-locscale-gamlss with a cubic B-spline basis of 12 columns for each predictor — knots at income quantiles, second-difference penalties (@def-smo-pspline) — and measure income and food expenditure in thousands of francs. The two smoothing parameters are chosen by ten-fold cross-validation of the log score over a grid, giving 31.6 for the mean and 10.0 for the scale, with effective degrees of freedom 8.75 and 5.59, 14.33 in all.

The fitted scale rises from 40.5 francs at an income of 500 to 184.5 at an income of 2000, a ratio of 4.55; the single constant the homoscedastic model fits is 107.4 francs, wrong in both directions at once. At an income of 1000 francs the fitted mean budget is 645.3 francs and the fitted ninetieth percentile 746.5. With the response in thousands of francs the AIC is −526.1 against −368.0 for the same mean spline with a constant scale, and the cross-validated log score −1.1102 against −0.6938: most of what a homoscedastic model gets wrong here is the scale. The implied quantile curves μ^(x)+σ^(x)zτ cannot cross, one clear advantage over the separate fits of Section 45.3.

exm-qnt-expectile-levels.title: Which quantile is the nine-tenths expectile?
exm-qnt-expectile-levels.title_html: Which quantile is the nine-tenths expectile?
exm-qnt-expectile-levels.html: For a standard normal the 0.9-expectile sits at the 0.806-quantile and the 0.5-expectile at the 0.500-quantile, as symmetry requires. For a lognormal with log-scale 0.8 the 0.9-expectile sits at the 0.892-quantile: the heavy right tail drags it further out. For the residuals of the least squares fit to Engel’s budgets the 0.9-expectile sits at the 0.851-quantile and the 0.1-expectile at the 0.170-quantile (Figure 45.4.1(b)). Three distributions, three answers to the same question.

exm-qnt-lp.title: Seven quantile lines for Engel’s budgets
exm-qnt-lp.title_html: Seven quantile lines for Engel’s budgets
exm-qnt-lp.html:
Fitting @eq-qnt-lp at seven levels gives slopes rising steadily with τ:

τ 0.05 0.10 0.25 0.50 0.75 0.90 0.95
slope 0.3434 0.4018 0.4741 0.5602 0.6440 0.6863 0.7091
intercept 124.9 110.1 95.5 81.5 62.4 67.4 64.1

The least squares slope, 0.4852, sits between the quartiles. A household at the tenth percentile of its income group spends about 0.4018 of each extra franc on food, one at the ninetieth 0.6863; at an income of 1000 francs the fitted median budget share is 0.642 and the tenth-percentile share 0.512. Every fit interpolates 2 observations and satisfies @eq-qnt-counting, as the listings verify.

exm-qnt-normal-gamlss.title: The heteroscedastic normal model
exm-qnt-normal-gamlss.html:
The smallest interesting case has K=2, D=N(μ,σ2), identity link on μ and log link on σ: Yi∼N(μi,σi2),μi=ηi1,log⁡σi=ηi2.{#eq-qnt-locscale-gamlss}

The log link keeps σi>0 whatever the predictor does, as it kept a Poisson mean positive in Chapter 37. With both predictors linear this is @prp-qnt-beyond-mean(b) with normal ε; with penalized splines it is the fit of @exm-qnt-engel-gamlss.

exm-qnt-three-ses.title: Three standard errors for one slope
exm-qnt-three-ses.title_html: Three standard errors for one slope
exm-qnt-three-ses.html:
At τ=0.5 the fitted income slope is 0.5602, and the three routes give very different precisions:

method τ=0.5 τ=0.9
iid formula @eq-qnt-iid 0.0121 0.0143
sandwich @eq-qnt-sandwich 0.0308 0.0300
pairs bootstrap, B=999 0.0344 0.0264

At the median the iid formula is optimistic by a factor of 2.5 against the sandwich and rather more against the bootstrap, which is no surprise: @exm-qnt-engel-bands showed that these errors are anything but identically distributed. The least squares slope has standard error 0.0144 under the same false assumption. The estimated sparsity is 192.2 francs at τ=0.5 and 378.9 at τ=0.9.

exm-qnt-unbounded.title: Watching it happen
exm-qnt-unbounded.html: Fitting @eq-qnt-locscale-gamlss to Engel’s budgets with the scale penalty set to 0.01 instead of the chosen 10.0 raises the in-sample log-likelihood from 277.4 to 282.9, a gain a naive search would take. The ten-fold cross-validated log score — minus the mean predictive log density, so that smaller is better (@def-qnt-score and the remark in Section 45.6) — tells the truth: it moves from −1.1102 to 59.9. The wilder scale curve dips towards zero where the mean spline interpolates, and a held-out household near such a dip is assigned a density indistinguishable from zero.

exr-qnt-band-arithmetic.title: B2
exr-qnt-band-arithmetic.html: In @exm-qnt-engel-bands the homoscedastic 95% prediction interval has half-width close to 2×114.1 francs for every household. Using the within-third standard deviations, say roughly what nominal level that half-width actually attains in the poorest third and in the richest third, if the conditional law were normal with the within-third standard deviation. Comment on the direction of both errors.

exr-qnt-count-example.title: A1
exr-qnt-count-example.html: A quantile regression with an intercept and one regressor is fitted at τ=0.25 to n=40 observations. How many residuals can be negative, and how many are exactly zero? Use @prp-qnt-counts.

exr-qnt-crossing-two-lines.title: B2
exr-qnt-crossing-two-lines.html: Two fitted quantile lines a1+b1x and a2+b2x with b1<b2 cross at x∗=−(a2−a1)/(b2−b1). Using the numbers of @exm-qnt-lp, verify the crossing income of the τ=0.05 and τ=0.10 lines, and explain why @prp-qnt-crossing(a) guarantees that x∗ cannot lie at the mean income.

exr-qnt-crps-decomposition.title: C1
exr-qnt-crps-decomposition.html: Interpret the two terms of @eq-qnt-crps-decomposition. Show that the second depends only on the truth G, so it is an irreducible floor, and that the first is an integrated squared error between the forecast and the truth. Relate this to the bias-variance decomposition of prediction error in Section 29.1.

exr-qnt-crps-energy.title: B2
exr-qnt-crps-energy.html: Prove the identity used in @exr-qnt-crps-normal: CRPS(F,y)=E|X−y|−12E|X−X′| for independent X,X′∼F with finite mean.

exr-qnt-crps-normal.title: B1
exr-qnt-crps-normal.html: Show that for F=N(μ,σ2) and z=(y−μ)/σ, CRPS(F,y)=σ{z(2Φ(z)−1)+2φ(z)−1π}, using the identity CRPS(F,y)=E|X−y|−12E|X−X′| for independent X,X′∼F.

exr-qnt-expectile-heavy.title: C1
exr-qnt-expectile-heavy.html: Let Y have a Cauchy distribution. Which of the objects in this chapter still exist: the conditional mean, the τ-quantiles, the τ-expectiles? What does this say about the price of the smooth loss?

exr-qnt-expectile-normal.title: B1
exr-qnt-expectile-normal.html: For Y∼N(0,1), show that @eq-qnt-expectile-equation becomes τ{φ(μ)−μ(1−Φ(μ))}=(1−τ){φ(μ)+μΦ(μ)}, and verify numerically that μ0.9=0.8616 lies at the 0.806-quantile, as reported in @exm-qnt-expectile-levels.

exr-qnt-expectile-symmetry.title: B2
exr-qnt-expectile-symmetry.html: Show that if the law of Y is symmetric about m, then μτ+μ1−τ=2m, and that the τ-expectile lies at the α(τ)-quantile with α(1/2)=1/2. Does symmetry force α(τ)=τ?

exr-qnt-expectile-two-point.title: A1
exr-qnt-expectile-two-point.html: Let Y take the values 0 and 1 with probability 1/2 each. Compute μτ from @eq-qnt-expectile-equation as a function of τ, and compare with the τ-quantile.

exr-qnt-extreme.title: B1
exr-qnt-extreme.html: For a standard normal error law, compute τ(1−τ)s(τ)2 at τ=0.5,0.9,0.99 and confirm the claim in the warning above that precision deteriorates in the tail. At which τ is the factor smallest?

exr-qnt-gamlss-edf.title: A1
exr-qnt-gamlss-edf.html: In @exm-qnt-engel-gamlss the mean block has 12 basis columns and effective degrees of freedom 8.75. What are the two extreme values the effective degrees of freedom of that block could take, and which smoothing parameters produce them?

exr-qnt-gamlss-gamma.title: B1
exr-qnt-gamlss-gamma.html: For a gamma response with mean μ and shape ν, density d(y)={ν/μ}νyν−1e−νy/μ/Γ(ν), with log links on both parameters, compute ui1 and wi1 of @thm-qnt-gamlss(b) for the mean block. Is the model orthogonal in the sense of part (c)?

exr-qnt-gamlss-orthogonality.title: C1
exr-qnt-gamlss-orthogonality.html: Show that the normal family parameterized by (μ,σ) is orthogonal for any increasing link on σ, not just the logarithm, and find a parameterization of the normal family in which it is not. What does orthogonality buy in @thm-qnt-gamlss(b)?

exr-qnt-gamlss-working.title: B2
exr-qnt-gamlss-working.html: Verify from @eq-qnt-normal-scores that the working response for the scale block of the normal location-scale model is zi2=log⁡σi+12{(yi−μi)2/σi2−1}, and show that the scale step is therefore an ordinary penalized least squares smooth of the squared standardized residuals, shifted and halved.

exr-qnt-knight-mean.title: C1
exr-qnt-knight-mean.html: Use @eq-qnt-knight to show that the estimating equation for 𝛃βτ in the population is 𝛃E{xψτ(Y−x⊤βτ)}=0, and that this is the exact analogue of the normal equations with ψτ in place of the identity. Compare with the estimating-function framework of Chapter 38 (@def-ql-quasi): is ψτ a quasi-score?

exr-qnt-lognormal-shape.title: B1
exr-qnt-lognormal-shape.html: Let log⁡Y∣x∼N(α+βx, σ2) with σ constant. Show that the conditional quantiles of Y are not parallel, that the conditional coefficient of variation is constant, and that the conditional skewness is constant. Which parts of @prp-qnt-beyond-mean apply to Y, and which to log⁡Y?

exr-qnt-lp-dual.title: B2
exr-qnt-lp-dual.html: Write down the dual of the linear program @eq-qnt-lp and show that it is maxdy⊤dsubject toX⊤d=0,  d∈[τ−1,τ]n, or, after the shift a=d+(1−τ)1, max{y⊤a:X⊤a=(1−τ)X⊤1, a∈[0,1]n}. Show that at an optimum ai=1 for a positive residual and ai=0 for a negative one, so that a records the “signs” of the residuals, and explain why these are the raw material of the rank tests of Section 45.3.

exr-qnt-normal-median.title: A1
exr-qnt-normal-median.html: Use @eq-qnt-iid to show that for iid normal errors the asymptotic variance of a regression median exceeds that of least squares by the factor π/2. Which assumption of @thm-qnt-asymptotics is doing the work?

exr-qnt-parallel.title: A1
exr-qnt-parallel.html: In a homoscedastic linear model with normal errors, by how much does the 0.9 conditional quantile exceed the 0.5 conditional quantile? Show that the answer does not depend on x, and say which part of @prp-qnt-beyond-mean this illustrates.

exr-qnt-pit-shapes.title: A1
exr-qnt-pit-shapes.html: A forecaster issues N(0,4) every day while the truth is N(0,1). Sketch the probability integral transform histogram, and say which of the four shapes listed above appears.

exr-qnt-sample-quantile.title: B1
exr-qnt-sample-quantile.html: Take X=1, so that the problem is to fit one number. Show that the minimizers of ∑iρτ(yi−b) are exactly the τ-quantiles of the empirical distribution of y1,…,yn, and that for τn not an integer the minimizer is the unique order statistic y(⌈τn⌉).

exr-qnt-uniqueness.title: C1
exr-qnt-uniqueness.html: Show that the set of minimizers of Rτ is a convex polyhedron, and that if it contains two distinct points then Rτ is constant on the segment joining them. Deduce that a unique solution is the generic case: non-uniqueness requires a coincidence in the data, such as p+1 observations lying on one hyperplane.

lem-qnt-knight.title: Knight’s identity
lem-qnt-knight.html: For all real u and v, with ψτ(u)=τ−1{u<0}, ρτ(u−v)−ρτ(u)=−vψτ(u)+∫0v{1{u≤s}−1{u≤0}}ds.{#eq-qnt-knight}

lem-qnt-monotone.title: Quantiles follow monotone maps
lem-qnt-monotone.html: Let Y be a random variable and h a strictly increasing, left-continuous function on the range of Y. Then Qh(Y)(τ)=h(QY(τ)) for every τ∈(0,1).

prp-qnt-beyond-mean.title: What a mean model does and does not say
prp-qnt-beyond-mean.title_html: What a mean model does and does not say
prp-qnt-beyond-mean.html:
Let x be a covariate vector and ε a random variable with quantile function qε, independent of x.

  1. Location model. If 𝛃Y=x⊤β+ε, then 𝛃QY(τ∣x)=x⊤β+qε(τ). Every conditional quantile curve is the regression curve shifted by a constant, so the effect of a covariate on the τ-quantile is 𝛃β, the same for every τ, and the conditional distribution has the same shape and the same spread everywhere.

  2. Location-scale model. If 𝛃𝛂Y=x⊤β+exp⁡(x⊤α)ε, then 𝛃𝛂QY(τ∣x)=x⊤β+exp⁡(x⊤α)qε(τ),{#eq-qnt-locscale}

    so 𝛃𝛂𝛂∂QY(τ∣x)/∂x=β+qε(τ)exp⁡(x⊤α)α does depend on τ. The quantile curves are no longer parallel, but they are still generated by one curve qε stretched by one positive function.

  3. Beyond scale. In (b) the standardized response 𝛃𝛂{Y−x⊤β}exp⁡(−x⊤α) has a distribution free of x. Any feature of the conditional law that is invariant under location and scale changes — skewness, kurtosis, the ratio of any two central moments of the same degree — is therefore constant in x. A model of the mean and the variance cannot represent a conditional distribution whose shape moves with x.

prp-qnt-comparison.title: The continuous ranked probability score and the probability integral transform
prp-qnt-comparison.title_html:
The continuous ranked probability score and the probability integral
transform
prp-qnt-comparison.html:
For a distribution function F with finite mean and a real y, define CRPS(F,y)=∫−∞∞{F(s)−1{y≤s}}2ds.{#eq-qnt-crps}

  1. CRPS(F,y) is finite, and for any G with finite mean EY∼GCRPS(F,Y)=∫{F(s)−G(s)}2ds+∫G(s){1−G(s)}ds.{#eq-qnt-crps-decomposition}

    Hence the CRPS is a strictly proper scoring rule on the distributions with finite mean.

  2. If F is continuous and strictly increasing with finite mean, then CRPS(F,y)=2∫01ρτ{y−F−1(τ)}dτ:{#eq-qnt-crps-check}

    the CRPS is the check loss averaged over all levels.

  3. If Y∼F with F continuous, then U=F(Y) is uniform on (0,1). If the predictive distributions F1,…,Fn are the true conditional distributions of independent Y1,…,Yn and each is continuous, then the probability integral transforms Ui=Fi(Yi) are independent and uniform.

prp-qnt-counts.title: Interpolation and counting
prp-qnt-counts.html:
Let rank(X)=p and let 𝛃β^τ minimize @eq-qnt-sample.

  1. There is a minimizer whose residual vector vanishes at p observations whose rows of X are linearly independent: the fit passes exactly through p of the data points.

  2. If 1∈C(X), then for any minimizer, with n−,n0,n+ the numbers of negative, zero and positive residuals, n−≤τn≤n−+n0.{#eq-qnt-counting}

prp-qnt-crossing.title: Ordering, and how to restore it
prp-qnt-crossing.title_html: Ordering, and how to restore it
prp-qnt-crossing.html:
1. Let x¯=n−1∑ix(i) and let 𝛃β^τ solve @eq-qnt-sample. Then 𝛃τ↦x¯⊤β^τ is nondecreasing: at the average design point the fitted quantiles never cross.

  2. Fix x and levels τ1<⋯<τm, let 𝛃qj=x⊤β^τj be the fitted values and let q(1)≤⋯≤q(m) be the same numbers sorted. For any nondecreasing sequence g1≤⋯≤gm and any p≥1, ∑j=1m|q(j)−gj|p≤∑j=1m|qj−gj|p.{#eq-qnt-rearrange}

    Sorting the fitted quantiles therefore moves them no further from the true quantile curve, in every Lp sense at once.

prp-qnt-expectile.title: Properties of expectiles
prp-qnt-expectile.html:
Let EY2<∞ and let Y be non-degenerate.

  1. Existence, uniqueness, monotonicity. S is finite, differentiable and strictly convex, and μτ is its unique stationary point, characterized by τE(Y−μτ)+=(1−τ)E(μτ−Y)+.{#eq-qnt-expectile-equation}

    The map τ↦μτ is strictly increasing on (0,1).

  2. The mean is an expectile. μ1/2=EY.

  3. The level of a point. For every μ with P(Y<μ)>0 and P(Y>μ)>0 — equivalently, every μ interior to the convex hull of the support of Y — there is exactly one τ with μτ=μ, namely τ=E(μ−Y)+E|Y−μ|.{#eq-qnt-expectile-level}

  4. Equivariance. For a>0 and b∈R, μτ(aY+b)=aμτ(Y)+b, and μτ(−Y)=−μ1−τ(Y). Expectiles are not equivariant under nonlinear increasing transformations.

prp-qnt-iwls.title: The estimating equation and its iteration
prp-qnt-iwls.title_html: The estimating equation and its iteration
prp-qnt-iwls.html:
Let rank(X)=p and Q(b)=∑iρτE(yi−x(i)⊤b).

  1. Q is continuously differentiable and strictly convex, so it has a unique minimizer, characterized by X⊤W(b)(y−Xb)=0,W(b)=diag{wi(b)},wi(b)=|τ−1{yi<x(i)⊤b}|.{#eq-qnt-expectile-normal}

  2. The iterated weighted least squares step b(t+1)={X⊤W(b(t))X}−1X⊤W(b(t))y has the property that if W(b(t+1))=W(b(t)), then b(t+1) is the exact global minimizer of Q.

thm-qnt-asymptotics.title: Asymptotic normality of a regression quantile
thm-qnt-asymptotics.title_html: Asymptotic normality of a regression quantile
thm-qnt-asymptotics.html:
Fix τ and suppose the rows x(i) are fixed and the errors 𝛃ui=yi−x(i)⊤βτ are independent with distribution functions Fi satisfying Fi(0)=τ. Assume

  1. each Fi has a density fi in a neighbourhood of zero with fi(0)>0; the fi are equicontinuous at zero, that is supisup|s|≤t|fi(s)−fi(0)|→0 as t↓0; and supisup|s|<ϵfi(s)<∞ for some ϵ>0;

  2. n−1∑ix(i)x(i)⊤→D0 and n−1∑ifi(0)x(i)x(i)⊤→D1, both positive definite;

  3. n−1/2maxi‖x(i)‖→0.

Then 𝛃𝛃n(β^τ−βτ)→dNp(0,τ(1−τ)D1−1D0D1−1).{#eq-qnt-sandwich}

If the errors are identically distributed with density f, then D1=f(0)D0 and the covariance collapses to τ(1−τ)f(0)2D0−1=τ(1−τ)s(τ)2D0−1,s(τ)=1f{F−1(τ)},{#eq-qnt-iid}

where s is the sparsity function, the derivative of the quantile function.

thm-qnt-check.title: The check loss elicits the quantile
thm-qnt-check.title_html: The check loss elicits the quantile
thm-qnt-check.html:
Let Y be a random variable with distribution function F and E|Y|<∞, and let G(q)=Eρτ(Y−q).

  1. Population characterization. G is finite and convex, and for q<q′ G(q′)−G(q)=∫qq′{F(s)−τ}ds.{#eq-qnt-difference}

    Consequently the set of minimizers of G is exactly the set of τ-quantiles of F, that is {q:F(q−)≤τ≤F(q)}.

  2. Linear program. Writing ui=(yi−x(i)⊤b)+ and vi=(x(i)⊤b−yi)+, problem @eq-qnt-sample is equivalent to minb,u,v{τ1⊤u+(1−τ)1⊤v}subject toXb+u−v=y,  u≥0, v≥0,{#eq-qnt-lp}

    a linear program in 2n+2p nonnegative variables with n equality constraints.

  3. Equivariance of the estimate. Let 𝛃β^τ(y,X) denote any solution of @eq-qnt-sample. For a>0, 𝛄γ∈Rp and nonsingular A, 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛄𝛃𝛄𝛃𝛃β^τ(ay,X)=aβ^τ(y,X),β^τ(−y,X)=−β^1−τ(y,X),β^τ(y+Xγ,X)=β^τ(y,X)+γ,β^τ(y,XA)=A−1β^τ(y,X).

  4. Equivariance under monotone maps. For strictly increasing left-continuous h, Qh(Y)(τ∣x)=h{QY(τ∣x)}.

thm-qnt-gamlss.title: Penalized likelihood and block-wise Fisher scoring
thm-qnt-gamlss.title_html: Penalized likelihood and block-wise Fisher scoring
thm-qnt-gamlss.html:
Write 𝛉ℓi(θi)=log⁡d(yi;θi1,…,θiK) and collect the coefficients of predictor k into 𝛄γk with design Zk, penalty matrix Pk and smoothing parameter λk, so that 𝛈𝛄ηk=Zkγk. The penalized log-likelihood is 𝛄𝛄𝛉𝛄𝛄ℓp(γ1,…,γK)=∑i=1nℓi(θi)−12∑k=1Kλkγk⊤Pkγk.{#eq-qnt-penalized-loglik}

  1. Score. With uik=∂ℓi/∂ηik and uk=(u1k,…,unk)⊤, 𝛄𝛄∂ℓp∂γk=Zk⊤uk−λkPkγk.{#eq-qnt-gamlss-score}

  2. Fisher scoring is penalized weighted least squares. Let wik=−E(∂2ℓi/∂ηik2) and Wk=diag(w1k,…,wnk). Updating block k with the others held fixed by one Fisher scoring step gives 𝛄𝛈γknew=(Zk⊤WkZk+λkPk)−1Zk⊤Wkzk,zk=ηk+Wk−1uk,{#eq-qnt-gamlss-step}

    the penalized version of the iteratively reweighted least squares of @thm-glm-irls, with zk the working response for parameter k. Cycling over k=1,…,K until nothing changes is backfitting (@thm-add-backfitting) applied to the K blocks.

  3. The normal location-scale model is orthogonal. For @eq-qnt-locscale-gamlss, ui1=yi−μiσi2,wi1=1σi2,ui2=(yi−μi)2σi2−1,wi2=2,{#eq-qnt-normal-scores}

    and the expected cross-information −E(∂2ℓi/∂ηi1∂ηi2) is zero. The two blocks are therefore orthogonal: neither Fisher scoring step needs the other’s derivatives, the working response for μ is z1=y, and the working response for log⁡σ is 𝛈z2=η2+12u2.
